title: Solve an integral equation by an operator series
promptMarkdown: On $X=C([0,1])$ with the sup norm let $(Tf)(x)=\int_0^x f(t)dt$. (a) Prove for $n\ge1$ that $(T^nf)(x)=\frac1{(n-1)!}\int_0^x(x-t)^{n-1}f(t)dt$ and $\|T^n\|=1/n!$. (b) For every real or complex $\lambda$, prove $\sum_{n=0}^\infty\lambda^nT^n$ converges in operator norm and is a two-sided inverse of $I-\lambda T$. State the completeness used. (c) Deduce existence, uniqueness and the bound $\|f\|_\infty\le e^{|\lambda|}\|g\|_\infty$ for $f-\lambda Tf=g$. (d) Show evaluation at a point is a bounded functional of norm 1 on $X$, and use it to bound $|f(x_0)|$. Why does the same evaluation fail to be bounded for the integral norm on continuous functions?
hintLadder: Compute $T^2$ first on a triangular integration region.
Retain the factorial when estimating the operator series.
Multiply finite partial sums before passing to the norm limit.
For evaluation in the integral norm, concentrate a continuous tent at the fixed point.
